title: Threat Detection Library - Windows Endpoint Gap-Fill Detection Entry
description: Schema for a single detection entry in data/windows-endpoint-detections.json. Like the Cisco Network Device catalogue, this catalogue was built with a specific, documented methodology: every entry closes a gap identified by diffing this library against data/mitre-attack-windows.json (MITRE ATT&CK's official Detection Analytics for the 'Windows' platform) -- specifically the portion of that gap not already closed by the existing AD/RDP/DHCP catalogues or by the ESCU catalogue's 'Windows Endpoint'/'Windows Network Telemetry' components. Every entry's mitre_analytics[] field cites the specific official MITRE Detection Analytic ID(s) it is grounded in, the same provenance pattern used by the ESXi and Cisco MITRE-driven gap-fill batches.

id.description: Namespaced sequential ID, one namespace per primary MITRE tactic -- the same fifteen-namespace convention the Splunk ESCU and Cisco catalogues use.

component.description: Single value: this catalogue's whole scope is generic Windows OS endpoint telemetry (registry, process, file, service, WMI, security-log), the same telemetry domain as ESCU's 'Windows Endpoint' component, whose gap this catalogue closes.

detection_type.description: Uses the same TTP/Anomaly/Hunting/Correlation vocabulary as the Splunk ESCU and Cisco catalogues, since this catalogue is built from the same MITRE Detection Analytic source material.

mitre_analytics.description: Provenance link(s) to the official MITRE ATT&CK Detection Analytic(s) (data/mitre-attack-windows.json) this entry is grounded in -- same field shape as the ESXi and Cisco catalogues' MITRE-driven gap-fill batches (id = the analytic's ANnnnn identifier, name = its parent Detection Strategy's descriptive name).

threat_reference.description: Optional citation to a real, MITRE-documented campaign, intrusion set, or malware family this technique is directly associated with, verified against that STIX object's own MITRE 'uses' relationship.
